subject: DeployOps: on‑prem cluster wiring, VLAN bonding & storage fallback plan
body:
From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@physionics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: On‑prem cluster preflight: VLANs, NIC bonding, SR‑IOV and storage fallback

Hi team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the statement of work. Before we lock compute SKUs we need to confirm a few hardware + network design constraints so we can finalize procurement and the install window:

- We plan Mellanox/ConnectX‑6 NICs on all nodes; are there any special driver/kernel requirements for your runtime (e.g., UMA/OPA driver versions)?
- We want two physical NICs per host bonded (LACP) with VLANs: mgmt (VLAN 10), data/serving (VLAN 20), storage replication (VLAN 30). Any concerns with MTU=9000 across the fabric?
- For GPU nodes we want SR‑IOV for passthrough to pods. Is that supported with your recommended CNI and device-plugin?
- Storage fallback: primary plan is local NVMe for cache + iSCSI/NetApp for persistent volumes. In failure mode we need automatic remounting to remote blockstore and consistent PVC handoff. Any recommended provisioning strategy (local PersistentVolumes + static-provisioner, or CSI that supports topology+fallback)?

Attaching a preliminary network diagram and the procurement spec.

[Attachment: physionics-network-diagram-v2.pdf]
[Attachment: mellanox-compat.csv]

Can we get a quick call tomorrow? Ideally we want a canary plan (2 racks) + rollout timeline by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Marco Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure, Physionics
ops-infra@physionics.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: On‑prem cluster preflight: VLANs, NIC bonding, SR‑IOV and storage fallback

Hi Marco — thanks, good level of detail. Looping in Irene Choi from Field Operations for rack/network constraints.

Short answers up front:
- Mellanox ConnectX‑6 looks fine; we'll target drivers in the 5.x kernel family. We'll validate exact driver build as part of preflight (we have a compatibility matrix).
- MTU 9000 is acceptable but we require end‑to‑end jumbo frames across top-of-rack and spine; we will test with iperf during canary.
- SR‑IOV + GPUs: supported, but gating condition is hypervisor/firmware on the host and that SR‑IOV VF counts match GPU topology. We'll include a VF map in the nodeclass doc.
- Storage fallback strategy: our recommendation is a two‑tier PV model:
  * Nodeclass "gpu-hot" — local NVMe as an ephemeral cache using local PersistentVolumes (local‑pv + static‑provisioner) for fastest inference hot path.
  * Nodeclass "stable-block" — remote encrypted blockstore (iSCSI or CSI to NetApp/Ceph) for critical stateful workloads.

For automatic failover between tiers we rely on higher‑level controller logic (we can provide a small operator that rewrites PVCs to the remote class on node failure and triggers a controlled rollout). That avoids brittle, cross‑filesystem remount hacks.

Attachments I will circulate: nodeclass matrix (initial), and a short runbook for canary rollouts.

Propose a quick sync 2026‑12‑22 09:00 PT (30m). I’ll send a calendar invite.

- Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Customer Solutions — Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: On‑prem cluster preflight: VLANs, NIC bonding, SR‑IOV and storage fallback

Great thread — a couple of engineering specifics to call out for the canary: 

1) Bonding / VLANs - Use LACP (802.3ad) active mode with bonding mode 4. Verify switch side supports LAG across the two NICs per host (we prefer single‑node LAG to avoid multi‑chassis LAG complexity). - MTU 9000 ok, but set dev mtu on bond and on the physical NICs; Calico in BGP mode preserves MTU, flannel VXLAN will fragment so avoid VXLAN for data plane.

2) CNI + SR‑IOV - Recommend Calico with host‑routing for data plane and calico‑policy for network policies. For SR‑IOV we use the standard sriov‑network‑device‑plugin + device‑plugin config maps. We’ll provide the device plugin manifests tuned for ConnectX‑6.

3) Storage topology - Prefer remote blockstore for any PVCs that need durability (RWO/RWX patterns depend on backend). For DB or metadata store use iSCSI/NetApp (multipath) or Ceph RBD for better performance and reattach semantics. - For NVMe local caching: use Kubernetes Local PersistentVolume with topology constraints and a static-provisioner. To allow fallback, we implement a reconciler (operator) that observes node termination and migrates workload by creating a new PVC bound to the remote storage class and patching Pod specs (or triggering rolling replacements). This avoids risky live remounts. - ReclaimPolicyRetention vs Delete: set Delete for ephemeral cache volumes; Retain for PVs that require manual recovery.

4) KMS / encryption - We can integrate with your KMS (Vault or cloud KMS) for envelope encryption of the blockstore. Key lifecycle + rotation needs to be part of acceptance tests.

5) Rollback / Canary - Canary: 2 racks (rack A, rack B) with identical configs; run synthetic load (inference trace) and fail one rack to test reconciling. - Eviction settings: kubelet.evictionHard memory.available=200Mi,nodefs.available=10% and set pod disruption budgets to control rollouts.

I’ll attach the nodeclass matrix and a short script we use to validate SR‑IOV availability during preflight.

- Dev
Dev Patel
Infra Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Action items:
- Dev: validate ConnectX‑6 firmware/driver against our SR‑IOV manifests and share a compatibility note (target: 2026‑12‑23 EOD).
- Irene: request VLAN tables and switch LAG config from Physionics DC (target: 2026‑12‑22 COB).
- Jasmine: share canary runbook + operator prototype for PVC fallback + calendar invite for 2026‑12‑22 09:00 PT (30m).
- Marco: confirm Mellanox part numbers and provide Rack/Topo diagrams with exact port mappings (target: 2026‑12‑23).

Acceptance criteria for canary:
- MTU validated end‑to‑end and iperf baseline captured.
- SR‑IOV enumerates expected VFs on GPU nodes and device‑plugin passes health checks.
- Local NVMe cache operates with expected eviction/repopulate behavior; remote blockstore rebind works in simulated node failure.
- KMS integration validated for PV secret encryption (Vault token + kube‑auth test).

Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.ai/rooms/deployops‑physionics‑1222
Attachments referenced: physionics-network-diagram-v2.pdf, k8s-nodeclass-matrix.xlsx, mellanox-compat.csv
